title: One implementation of the told-once late-end rule (in-turn path and reported-end path)
outcome: The rule "a late end under a closed check's key is told once and its closure retired" lives in one function, used both by note_engram_command_finished_with_capture's in-turn path and by note_engram_reported_end.
acceptance: C1. The in-turn late-end tell in note_engram_command_finished_with_capture calls engram_tell_late_end_of_closed_check, adapting its exit argument, and the duplicated guard, position/remove and publish are gone.
C2. The comments on EngramHost::codex_reported_end, codex_events' late-end handling and the engram_reported_ends.rs header describe the id-less hand-over and the told-once tell.
C3. Existing late-end tests (engram_unended_closures, silent_check_outcome, reported_ends) pass unchanged.

C4. A regression test drives one late end that reaches both paths: Codex reports it tagged with the active turn, so both take_shared_codex_late_command_end and the in-turn route see it. The holder is told exactly once.
C5. The review pair has no outstanding finding of Medium or higher; focused checks pass on the frozen input; it lands after w-1b4f.
